content.howTitle: How to compare two texts online

steps.title: Paste or open the original
steps.text: Put the first version in the Original text box. You can paste text, or open or drag and drop a file.

steps.title: Add the changed version
steps.text: Put the second version in the Changed text box. The comparison runs automatically as you type.

steps.title: Review the differences
steps.text: Removed lines are red, added lines are green, and the exact words that changed are highlighted inside each line.

features.title: Side-by-side or unified diff
features.text: Read changes in two columns, or switch to a single-column unified diff exactly like git diff.

features.title: Word-level highlights
features.text: See which words and characters changed within a line, not just which lines are different.

features.title: Compare files

features.title: Ignore whitespace and case

features.title: 100% private

legend: Red lines exist only in the original text: they were removed.
Green lines exist only in the changed text: they were added.
Darker highlights mark the exact words that changed inside a modified line.
Hunk headers such as @@ -12,7 +12,9 @@ give the starting line and number of lines in each version. Unchanged lines in between are collapsed; click Expand to show them.

faq.q: How do I compare two texts online?
faq.a: Paste the original text into the left box and the changed text into the right box. DiffDuo compares them instantly and highlights every difference: removed lines in red, added lines in green, and the exact changed words inside each line.
A diff checker (or diff tool) finds the differences between two versions of a text. It shows which lines were added, deleted or changed, the same way git diff shows changes in source code.

faq.q: Is my text uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. The comparison runs entirely in your browser, so your text and files never leave your device. This makes DiffDuo safe for confidential documents, code and configuration files.
Yes. Click Open or drag and drop a file onto either box. Any plain-text file works, including code, JSON, XML, YAML, CSV, SQL, Markdown, HTML and log files, up to 50 MB each.

faq.q: How do I ignore whitespace or capitalization differences?
faq.a: Turn on Ignore whitespace to treat lines as equal when they differ only in spaces, tabs or indentation, and Ignore case to ignore uppercase and lowercase differences.

faq.q: What is the difference between split and unified view?
faq.a: Split view shows the two texts side by side, which is easiest to read. Unified view shows a single column with removed lines marked with a minus and added lines marked with a plus, the same format as git diff and patch files.
Yes. DiffDuo compares files with hundreds of thousands of lines in a background thread, so the page stays responsive. Two 4 MB files with 100,000 lines each compare in well under a second.
Yes. DiffDuo is completely free, with no sign-up, no limits on the number of comparisons and no ads.
